thread:
ana: heads up — after today's SDK rollout i'm seeing a dozen timeout traces for short chat completions. pattern points to queueing in the connection pool rather than model slowness.
tom: same here. p95 latency for 256-byte prompts jumped from 90ms -> 420ms in Canary. Any config changes shipped?
jeremy: I checked the changelog: rw-python-sdk v1.5.2 included a change to 'fair_queue' scheduling and an idle-session trimming heuristic (PR #436). Could be interacting poorly with lots of tiny requests.
sophia: repro script I used (attached) — simulate many tiny requests that finish quickly so fairness matters:
```
# bench_small.py
async def task(client):
    for _ in range(500):
        await client.chat("hi")
```
run with `python bench_small.py --concurrency 400 --qps 800 --uvloop`
jeremy: On my laptop the failure mode is queue_len growing and steady inflight ~= 80 while queue keeps growing, then many requests hit client-side timeout. logs: 
```
2026-03-21T08:15:11Z WARN pool: acquired_wait=198ms queue_len=310 inflight=78 conf.max_connections=128
2026-03-21T08:15:11Z ERROR request=x77de timeout after 6s
```
ana: Interesting difference from previous thread — we saw semaphore-based prioritization starving longlived ops. This looks like fairness algorithm is favoring older queued tasks causing churn.
tom: Could also be connection recycle frequency. If SESSION_REAP_INTERVAL is too low re-establishing TLS on hot flows will cost us. What's default now?
jeremy: Default SESSION_REAP_INTERVAL=45 (seconds) after the change, before it was 300. That was lowered to save sockets in low-traffic tails. But with sustained high short requests it causes thrash.
sophia: Quick mitigation: set env RW_SDK_FAIR_QUEUE=false and RW_SESSION_REAP_INTERVAL=600 on canary — that brought p95 back to 120ms.
ops-bot: rolling config update to canary: RW_SDK_FAIR_QUEUE=false RW_SESSION_REAP_INTERVAL=600 (started 09:12 UTC)
tom: For the long term we should: 1) add a smoke integration test that sends high qps of tiny requests to catch regressions, 2) telemetry for queue_len and acquire_wait_ms, 3) document recommended defaults for SDK quickstart (we keep tripping on these envs during onboarding).
nana: I'll open issue with repro and logs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-python-sdk/issues/418 and include the bench script + datadog screenshots. Assigning to @jeremy and @tom.
jeremy: I'll draft a revert for the idle trimming change and instead add an adaptive reaper that increases threshold with short request ratio. Also will add a runtime flag `RW_ENABLE_FAIR_QUEUE=true` defaulted after we verify.
sophia: Add unit test that simulates a mix of short vs long requests and validates no starvation after 30s. Also add typing hints for PoolConfig (we saw a few callers passing ints vs strings) — that will reduce onboarding friction when people set envs via containers.
tom: Great. After the revert + tests we should publish a patch release and update the release notes with recommended envs for low-latency apps.
nana: Thanks team — canary looks stable after config patch. I'll follow up with a devex doc update for the quickstart and a sample showing recommended pool config for chat apps.
